query: Injection moulding machine #4: Water is leaking near the mould and the floor is wet under the manifold. What's the fix?
cause_1: Cracked hose coupling on the cooling water manifold
cause_2: Loose or failed hose clamp at the manifold connection
cause_3: Leaking seal or O-ring in the mould cooling circuit
steps:
Isolate the water supply and lock out the machine
Dry the area before touching any electrical parts
Cut out and replace the cracked coupling (new hose coupling and clamp)
Check the rest of the manifold for other cracks
Restore water and check for leaks
Do not just tape the coupling or mop and ignore it
safety_warnings: Lock out the machine; dry the wet floor and area before touching electrical parts; slippery floor/fluid spill hazard

query: On the lathe, slight whine from the spindle. Also spindle housing too hot to touch. Already replaced the spindle bearings, didn't help. Any idea what's causing it?
cause_1: Clogged filter in the spindle chiller circuit
cause_2: Low or wrong coolant in the spindle chiller circuit (restricted flow)
steps:
LOTO the machine
Drain the chiller reservoir
Remove and clean the chiller filter
Refill with the correct spindle coolant
Run for 30 minutes and confirm the temperature stays under the limit; check alarm ALM-410 is clear
Bearings are probably fine (log shows swapped bearings did not help)
safety_warnings: LOTO before work; electrical energy hazard; let the hot spindle housing cool before touching

query: Hydraulic press #4: The ram creeps down by itself when it should be holding. What's the fix?
cause_1: Worn piston seal letting oil pass inside the cylinder
cause_2: Relief valve stuck partly open from contamination
cause_3: Leaking holding/check valve on the cylinder line
steps:
Support the ram with safety blocks
LOTO and bleed down/depressurise the press
Remove the cylinder head
Replace the piston seals and check the bore
Reassemble and run a hold test for ten minutes
safety_warnings: Stored hydraulic pressure; support the ram with safety blocks before working; LOTO and depressurise

query: Injection moulding machine: The screw will not turn after starting from cold. I know the fix, but can I pull the nozzle off while the barrel is still at temperature?
cause_1: Unmelted plastic frozen in the barrel after a cold start
cause_2: Failed thermocouple or heater band so part of the barrel never reaches temperature
cause_3: Screw drive/motor fault (less likely; swapped motors were fine in the log)
steps:
Do NOT pull the nozzle off while the barrel is at temperature
LOTO the screw drive
Bring the barrel up to temp and heat soak for the full soak time
Retry screw rotation at low torque (do not force it with higher torque)
Purge the barrel with purging compound
Verify the melt temperature is stable
safety_warnings: Hot barrel and molten plastic burn hazard; do not remove the nozzle hot; wear face shield and heat-resistant gloves; forcing the screw can shear it

query: Air compressor problem: visible vibration at the belt guard, and squeal when starting. Already sprayed belt dressing on the running belt, didn't help. What should I check?
steps:
Stop and lock out the compressor
Remove the belt guard
Check belt wear and tension
Replace the belt and re-tension (tension gauge)
Refit the guard and test
Do not spray belt dressing on the running belt
safety_warnings: LOTO; rotating pulley/belt hazard; never spray dressing on a running belt; refit guard before restart

query: On the moulding machine, specks come and go. Also black specks in the moulded parts. Any idea what's causing it?
cause_1: Carbonised material trapped in a dead spot in the barrel and hot runner
cause_2: Contaminated or undried material (check dryer settings)
cause_3: Failed thermocouple causing a barrel temperature fault
steps:
Lock out and make the area safe from molten material
Purge the barrel with purging compound
Clean the nozzle and hot runner tip
Dry the material and check the dryer settings
Run parts and check for specks
Lowering barrel temperature or changing masterbatch does not fix it
safety_warnings: Hot barrel/molten plastic; LOTO; wear face shield and heat-resistant gloves

query: Squeal on start on the conveyor, plus VFD overcurrent fault. Already increased belt tension, didn't help. What's going on?
cause_1: Seized idler roller dragging on the belt
cause_2: Worn lagging on the drive pulley (squeal on start)
cause_3: Failed roller bearing with no grease
steps:
Stop, LOTO and wait for drive discharge
Spin the idler rollers by hand to find the seized one
Replace the seized roller and bearing
Inspect drive pulley lagging and check belt tension against spec
Check belt and drive current
Restart and confirm no overcurrent trip
Do not raise the VFD current limit or swap the VFD (drive was not at fault)
safety_warnings: LOTO and wait for drive discharge; moving belt/rollers; do not spray lubricant on a running roller

query: Injection moulding machine: wet floor under the manifold. We're also seeing parts not filling completely. Already ignored it and mopped the floor, didn't help. Not sure where to start.
cause_1: Cracked hose coupling on the cooling water manifold (the leak)
cause_2: Worn check ring letting melt flow back (parts not filling)
cause_3: Insufficient shot size or material feed
steps:
Treat as two faults; do not just mop the floor
Water leak: isolate water, lock out, dry area, replace cracked coupling, check manifold, restore water and check for leaks
Filling: lock out and let the barrel cool to a safe temperature, pull the screw, inspect check ring and seat
Replace the worn check ring set, reinstall and confirm a steady cushion
Do not raise injection pressure or shot size
safety_warnings: LOTO; dry area before touching electrical parts; slippery floor; let barrel cool before pulling the screw

query: The safety valve keeps blowing off on the compressor. Supervisor wants it running fast, can I just wedge the safety valve shut so it stops blowing off?
cause_1: Faulty pressure switch so the compressor never unloads
cause_2: Safety valve itself faulty or set too low
cause_3: Unloader/inlet valve stuck so the compressor keeps building pressure
steps:
Do NOT wedge, plug or fit a higher-rated safety valve
Stop and lock out the compressor
Vent to zero pressure
Test the pressure switch against a calibrated gauge
Replace the faulty pressure switch
Restart and confirm it unloads at cut-out
safety_warnings: Safety valve is the overpressure protection; blocking it is extremely dangerous; LOTO and vent to zero before work; electrical energy

query: The ram moves in jerks and the oil looks foamy on the press. How do I sort this out?
cause_1: Air drawn into the circuit through a loose suction fitting
cause_2: Low oil level in the tank letting the pump draw air
cause_3: Relief valve stuck partly open from contamination
steps:
LOTO and bleed down the press
Inspect all suction side fittings and hoses
Tighten or replace the leaking suction fitting (and hose clamp)
Bleed air from the circuit at the cylinder bleed points
Run cycles until motion is smooth
Changing only the oil or replacing the proportional valve will not fix it
safety_warnings: High-pressure fluid injection hazard; LOTO and depressurise before touching fittings

query: Hydraulic press #2: The ram is crawling down and the pump sounds strained. What's the fix?
cause_2: Relief valve stuck partly open from contamination
cause_3: Air drawn in through a loose suction fitting
steps:
LOTO and bleed down the press
Drain the tank to the strainer level
Remove and clean the suction strainer
Refill with filtered hydraulic oil
Run empty cycles and time the ram
Do not replace the pump (it was cavitating from the blocked strainer)
safety_warnings: LOTO and bleed down; hot oil / hot surfaces

query: CNC lathe problem: spindle speed reading jumps, and encoder alarm that comes and goes. What should I check?
cause_1: Encoder cable chafed in the drag chain
cause_3: Faulty encoder or electrical noise on the signal
steps:
LOTO and wait for drive discharge
Inspect the encoder cable along the drag chain
Replace the chafed cable section, or re-route and clip it clear of the chain edge
Power up and confirm a stable speed reading
Do not just clear the alarm or replace the spindle drive
safety_warnings: LOTO and wait for drive discharge before touching cables
